title: Find Products with Valid Serial Numbers
statement:
One table lists products:

- `products(product_id, product_name, description)`: one row per product; `product_id` is unique. `description` is free text.

A product qualifies when its description contains a valid serial number somewhere (not necessarily at the start). A valid serial number is:

- the letters `SN`, uppercase exactly (`sn` or `Sn` do not count);
- then exactly 4 digits, a hyphen `-`, and exactly 4 digits;
- a word of its own: the character just before `S` and the character just after the last digit, where they exist, are not a letter, a digit or `_`. So `SN1234-56789` and `XSN1234-5678` do not count, while `(SN1234-5678)` does.

Report `product_id`, `product_name` and `description` of every qualifying product, ordered by `product_id` ascending.
constraints: SN must be uppercase; the digits are 0-9
A serial number must not touch a letter, digit or underscore on either side
reference:
SELECT product_id, product_name, description
FROM products
WHERE REGEXP_LIKE(description, '\\bSN[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}\\b', 'c')
ORDER BY product_id;
brute:
WITH RECURSIVE pos AS (
  SELECT 1 AS p
  UNION ALL
  SELECT p + 1 FROM pos WHERE p < (SELECT MAX(CHAR_LENGTH(description)) FROM products)
)
SELECT DISTINCT pr.product_id, pr.product_name, pr.description
FROM products AS pr
JOIN pos ON pos.p + 10 <= CHAR_LENGTH(pr.description)
WHERE ASCII(SUBSTRING(pr.description, pos.p, 1)) = 83
  AND ASCII(SUBSTRING(pr.description, pos.p + 1, 1)) = 78
  AND SUBSTRING(pr.description, pos.p + 2, 9) REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}$'
  AND (pos.p = 1 OR SUBSTRING(pr.description, pos.p - 1, 1) NOT REGEXP '[A-Za-z0-9_]')
  AND SUBSTRING(pr.description, pos.p + 11, 1) NOT REGEXP '[A-Za-z0-9_]'
ORDER BY pr.product_id

notes:
## Intuition

The rule is a text shape, which is exactly what a regular expression describes: `SN`, four digits, a hyphen, four digits. Two details decide most cases. "Exactly four digits" means the pattern must not continue into a fifth digit or start after a stray letter, which the word boundary `\b` handles on both sides. And `SN` must be uppercase, while MySQL's `REGEXP` ignores case under the default collation, so the match needs the case-sensitive flag `'c'`.

## Approach

1. Read every row of `products`.
2. Keep a row when `REGEXP_LIKE(description, '\\bSN[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}\\b', 'c')` is 1. The pattern reads: a word boundary, `SN`, four digits, `-`, four digits, a word boundary. The pattern is unanchored, so the serial may sit anywhere in the text.
3. Return the three columns ordered by `product_id`.

## Example 1, step by step

- Product 1: `... with SN1234-5678` ends right after the last digit, so the end of the text is the boundary. Kept.
- Product 2: `SN9876-1234` is surrounded by spaces. Kept.
- Product 3: `SN1234-56789` has a fifth digit after the hyphen; after `5678` comes `9`, so no boundary there. Dropped.
- Product 4: no `SN` at all. Dropped.
- Product 5: `SN4321-8765` between spaces. Kept.

The result is products 1, 2 and 5 in id order.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · L) for n products with descriptions of length L; the regex scans each text once.
- Space: O(k) for the k matching rows.

## Pitfalls

- `description REGEXP 'SN...'` without `'c'` (or `LIKE '%SN%'`) also accepts `sn1234-5678`, because MySQL compares text without case.
- Dropping the trailing `\b` accepts `SN1234-56789`; dropping the leading one accepts `XSN1234-5678`.
- `LIKE '%SN____-____%'` lets `_` match any character, letters and spaces included.
- In a MySQL string literal a backslash must be doubled, so `\b` is written `'\\b'`.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `REGEXP_LIKE(text, pattern, 'c')` | 1 when `text` contains a match, comparing case exactly |
| `\b` | a word boundary: a letter, digit or `_` on one side only |
| `[0-9]{4}` | exactly four digits |

narration.1: The output is the product row itself, with its three columns unchanged.
narration.2: Every product is a candidate; there is nothing to join.
narration.3: REGEXP_LIKE with the c flag keeps rows whose description holds SN, four digits, a hyphen and four digits as a whole word, with SN in uppercase.
narration.4: The statement fixes the order: products by ascending id.
